info.description:
Clearstory's external customer API. Use it to read and manage projects,
contracts, change order requests, T&M tags, and the reference data that ties
them together.

New here? Start with the **Getting Started** guide below to create an API
application, get a token, and make your first request.
info.title: Clearstory API

post.description:
Creates a new attachment by uploading a file to Clearstory's storage. Send the request as multipart form data carrying the file and the `attachableType` and `attachmentType` fields, in any order. The stored file's metadata is created by Clearstory at upload time and should not be supplied.

Example form data:

- `attachmentType`: pdf
- `attachableType`: cors
- `attachableId`: 1714190
- `file`: COR-32.pdf

parameters.description: The file to upload. Select a PDF when `attachmentType` is `pdf`, or a JPEG or PNG when it is `image`
parameters.name: file

parameters.description: The type of entity this attachment will be associated with
parameters.name: attachableType

parameters.description: The category/type of the attachment being uploaded
parameters.name: attachmentType

parameters.description: The id of the entity this attachment will be associated with — send it to attach the file to a record, omit it to upload an unattached file. For COR attachments it must be a positive id of a COR that exists, is still a draft, and belongs to your company; for the other types it must reference a record of the given attachableType that belongs to your company
parameters.name: attachableId

post.description: Creates a draft Change Notification for a given project. Drafts created through this endpoint are not sent or submitted — contractors are not notified — and should be completed and sent from the web app. customerReferenceNumber is required and must be unique among the project's Change Notifications. Optionally pass contractIds (contractor contracts on the project) to stub the recipients. A 422 carries one of two shapes: field validation returns `{"success":false,"errors":[…]}` (ValidationErrorResponse); a business-rule rejection — unknown project, unknown contract, or a customerReferenceNumber already used on the project — returns `{"success":false,"message":"…"}` (BusinessErrorResponse).

get.description: Retrieves a list of Change Order Requests either sent or received by the company belonging to the requesting token, across all offices and projects. Sent records carry the customer object; received records carry the contract object. Each record's version is its revision number within the COR chain and originalCorId is the stable id of that chain. This list remains latest-only and does not include isLatestVersion. Note: for received CORs the top-level projectId is the sender's (contractor's) project, not yours — to match a received COR to your own project use contract.customerProjectId, or filter directly with companyJobNumber (e.g. ?inbox=received&companyJobNumber={jobNumber}).

get.description: Retrieves a Change Order Request that your company has sent or received by id or UUID. version is the revision number within the COR chain, originalCorId is the stable chain id, and isLatestVersion identifies the current stored revision. A known historical or draft revision can be retrieved directly by its own id or UUID. Note: for received CORs the top-level projectId is the sender's (contractor's) project, not yours — your own project is contract.customerProjectId.

parameters.description: The Change Order Request id or UUID
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Set true to include 3rd party integration metadata
parameters.name: withIntegrationMetadata

delete.description: Removes one or more labels from a Change Order Request. Label ids go in `labelIds` and label names in `labels`; both are optional and neither takes precedence — send either, both (the union of the two sets is removed), or neither. Unlike the add operation, an unknown label name is not created: ids and names that do not match one of your company's labels are skipped silently, and a request that names nothing removes nothing rather than failing. The Change Order Request including adjusted labels is returned.

parameters.description: The Change Order Request id or UUID
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Label ids and/or label names to remove. Both members are optional and are applied independently; omitting both removes nothing.
parameters.name: body

patch.description: Adds one or more labels to a Change Order Request. Label ids go in `labelIds` and label names in `labels`; both are optional and neither takes precedence — send either, both (the union of the two sets is added), or neither. Ids that do not belong to your company are skipped silently; names are always resolved within your company, and a name that does not exist yet is created and then added. A request that names nothing adds nothing rather than failing. The Change Order Request including adjusted labels is returned.

parameters.description: The Change Order Request id or UUID
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Label ids and/or label names to add. Both members are optional and are applied independently; omitting both adds nothing.
parameters.name: body

Each record keeps its own id and uuid, shares the stable originalCorId, includes the revision version, and adds isLatestVersion. The response uses CORSentRevision records for a contractor caller or CORReceivedRevision records for a customer caller. Draft revisions are omitted. Pagination uses the standard limit/offset parameters.

get.description: Retrieves a list of LMEO rates for a given project id. The record shape depends on rateType — `labor` returns ProjectLaborRate records, `material` ProjectMaterialRate, `equipment` ProjectEquipmentRate, and `other` ProjectOtherRate. The material, equipment, and other records carry `unit`, `rate`, `autoCalculateTotal`, and `standardAmount` in place of the labor rate fields; each shape is published under its own name in this document. The schema shown below is the `labor` one. An unrecognized rateType is rejected with a 422. A project that does not belong to your company yields an empty list (Node parity). Records expose projectRateId (this project-level record's id) and companyRateId (the company rate it was inherited from, null when created directly on the project); while inheritCompanyRateChanges is true the record continues to receive company-level rate updates.

parameters.name: projectId

post.description:
Creates a new T&M Tag draft. T&M Tags have an owner, and there is no requesting user to infer one from, so name the company user the tag belongs to in `creatorId`. The other association you need is the project the work was performed on, given as `projectId`; that project must already have a contract.

Every tag carries the list of customers and company users emailed when it is submitted. Omit `emailTo` and `emailCC` and Clearstory fills them in from the project's invited customers and company users. Send either key as an empty array to leave that list (To or CC) unset.

LMEO (labor, material, equipment, other) items can be created along with the tag; each type takes a slightly different, though similar, set of required fields. T&M Tags carry no pricing or rate information themselves, but an item can point back to an LMEO rate in the project's rate group through the optional `projectRateId`. With no rate associated, whoever turns the tag into a Change Order Request is prompted for a value — so pulling from the project's rates avoids manual data entry, though an item with no company rate behind it is perfectly valid.

Item descriptions can also be changed or customized independently of the rate they came from, which allows ad hoc adjustments while keeping the original rate association.

Files are attached separately: upload them with `POST /attachments` using `attachableType=tm_tags`.

parameters.description: The T&M Tag to create
parameters.name: body

get.description:
Retrieves an individual T&M Tag given its id. Visible to the contractor or the customer on the tag's contract.
The response always includes a nullable hcssTimecardId containing the source HCSS HeavyJob timecard ID; it is null for non-HCSS tags or unavailable metadata and is not the Clearstory tag number.

parameters.name: id

parameters.description: Set true to include 3rd party integration metadata
parameters.name: withIntegrationMetadata

delete.description: Removes an individual tag given its id. Only the company that created the tag can delete it.

parameters.description: The tag id
parameters.name: id

patch.description:
Updates a T&M Tag draft, modifying only the fields given. Note that a line-item key (`labor`, `material`, `equipment`, `other`) replaces the stored items of that type wholesale, so pass every existing item you want to keep whenever you send the key. Omitting the key leaves those items alone — it is a PATCH in that sense — but there is no shortcut for adding just one more labor item: send the existing ones along with the new one.

Note also that some fields cannot be updated, among them the project id and the creator (user) id.

parameters.description: The tag id
parameters.name: id

parameters.description: The T&M Tag fields to update
parameters.name: body

get.description: Retrieves users in the calling company, scoped by at most one of two optional filters. With no filter it returns the company's users (only users assigned to at least one active office). With projectId it returns the users assigned to that project, including users carried over from any project that was merged into it. With officeId it returns the users assigned to that office. projectId and officeId are mutually exclusive — sending both returns a 422 validation error. A project or office outside your company returns an empty list.

tags.description:
Welcome to the Clearstory API. Use it to read and manage projects, contracts, change order requests, T&M tags, and the reference data that ties them together.

**API URL:** `https://io.clearstory.build` — every endpoint below lives under the `/clearstory/v1` path.

V1 authenticates service accounts only (OAuth2 client credentials). User-level credentials with per-user permissions are coming in a later release.

## Authentication

Every request must carry an OAuth2 bearer token. Clearstory issues tokens
through the client-credentials flow, so no end user is involved once an
application has been set up.

### 1. Create an API application

In Clearstory, open **Settings > Advanced Settings > API Applications** and
create an application. The screen is available to Account Owners.

Clearstory shows the **client secret once**, at creation time — copy it then
and store it in your secret manager, because it cannot be retrieved
afterwards. The **client ID** stays visible in the applications list, and
deleting an application immediately revokes its access.

### 2. Exchange the credentials for a token

Request a token from Clearstory's authorization server. The `audience`
parameter is required and must match exactly.

```bash
curl -s https://auth.clearstory.build/oauth/token -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{
  "grant_type": "client_credentials",
  "client_id": "YOUR_CLIENT_ID",
  "client_secret": "YOUR_CLIENT_SECRET",
  "audience": "https://io.clearstory.build"
}'
```

The response carries an `access_token` and its `expires_in` lifetime, 24 hours
by default.

Cache the token for its full lifetime instead of requesting one per API call,
and refresh it with jitter rather than on a fixed schedule so your jobs do not
synchronize with every other integration. Retry token requests on HTTP 429
with backoff.

### 3. Call the API

Send the token on every request:

```bash
curl https://io.clearstory.build/clearstory/v1/company \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer YOUR_ACCESS_TOKEN' \
  -H 'User-Agent: my-integration/1.0'
```

A missing, expired, or malformed token is rejected with **401**. Requests also
need a non-blank `User-Agent` header identifying your integration; without one
the API responds **400**.
tags.name: Getting Started

tags.description:
Every paginated list endpoint pages the same way.

Pass `limit` (how many records, 1–100, default 50) and `offset` (how many to skip, ≥ 0, default 0). Values outside those ranges — including `limit=0` — return a 422 validation error rather than being clamped.

The legacy parameter names `take` and `skip` are accepted as aliases everywhere, so code written against the old API keeps working. When both a name and its alias are sent, `limit`/`offset` win.

Endpoints that accept `limit` and `offset` return the same envelope:

```json
{
  "count": 132,
  "offset": 0,
  "limit": 50,
  "records": [ ... ]
}
```

`count` is the total number of matching records, so `offset + limit < count` means there are more pages. One endpoint is an exception: on `GET /users` with neither `projectId` nor `officeId`, `count` deliberately ignores the active-office requirement the returned records honor — as the old API did — so it can be higher than the number of users you can actually page through.

Two list endpoints are not paginated: `GET /reason-categories` returns every reason category, with `count` and `records` but no `offset`/`limit`, and `GET /cors/{id}/line-items` returns a Change Order Request's line items grouped by type rather than in an envelope. Both still validate `limit` and `offset` — out-of-range or non-numeric values return the same 422 as anywhere else, because the check is applied to every endpoint — they just ignore valid ones.

Unlike the old API — which mixed `skip`/`take` and `limit`/`offset` conventions across endpoints with inconsistent edge behavior — these rules apply uniformly to every paginated list endpoint.
tags.name: Pagination

tags.description:
Build your integration to make efficient, well-paced use of the API. The practices below are what we expect of every client, and following them keeps your integration fast, resilient, and unaffected by future limits.

- **Cache your access token for its full lifetime.** Tokens are valid for 24 hours by default. Request a new one shortly before expiry — with a small amount of random jitter, so restarts and retries across your fleet don't synchronize — rather than requesting a token per API call. See [Getting Started](#tag/Getting-Started).
- **Back off and retry on `429 Too Many Requests`.** Use exponential backoff on both the token endpoint and the API, and honor the `Retry-After` header when a response carries one.
- **Sync incrementally rather than re-reading everything.** Most list endpoints accept `fromUpdatedAt` and `untilUpdatedAt`; record the timestamp of your last successful run and request only what changed since. Reference, aggregate, and sub-resource endpoints do not accept these filters: `GET /cors/overview`, `GET /cors/contract-summary`, `GET /cors/{id}/line-items`, and `GET /projects/{id}/integrations`.
- **Page through results with `limit` and `offset`** instead of repeatedly pulling the largest page you can. See [Pagination](#tag/Pagination).
- **Stagger scheduled work.** If your integration runs on a cron, avoid midnight UTC and the top of the hour, and spread requests across the window instead of bursting.
- **Request only what you need.** Filter server-side with the query parameters each endpoint documents rather than fetching broadly and discarding results in your own code.

Specific published limits are TBD and will be documented on this page. Building to the practices above means they should not require changes to your integration later.
tags.name: Rate Limiting

tags.description:
The Clearstory API is a new platform, not a drop-in replacement for the legacy API at `web-api.clearstory.build`. Response shapes are preserved wherever behavior didn't change, but the following differences are deliberate. Review each one before pointing existing integration code at the new API.

## Authentication

HTTP Basic Auth is replaced by OAuth2 client credentials. Exchange your `client_id`/`client_secret` for a bearer token — the `audience` parameter is required — and cache it for its full lifetime (24 hours by default). See [Getting Started](#tag/Getting-Started).

## Pagination

- `skip`/`take` are superseded by `offset`/`limit`. The old names still work as aliases on every endpoint.
- The valid `limit`/`take` range is strictly 1–100 (default 50). Out-of-range values — including `take=0`, which the old API answered inconsistently — now return a 422 validation error on every endpoint.

## Routes

- `GET /companies/current` is now `GET /company`.
- `GET /companies/current/offices` is now `GET /offices`.
- `GET /companies/current/divisions` is now `GET /divisions`.
- `GET /companies/current/users` is folded into `GET /users`, which now takes an optional `projectId` or `officeId` (mutually exclusive). With neither, it returns the company's users that are assigned to at least one active office — the same set the old `/companies/current/users` returned.
- Verify credentials with `GET /company`. The bare `GET /` smoke test is no longer part of the documented contract.

## Fields & parameters

- T&M tags: the documented spelling is now `subcontractorPrintedName`, with a lowercase "c", in create and update bodies. The old capitalization is no longer part of the contract and does not appear in responses or validation errors.
- LMEO Rates: filter by `internalId` (singular). The old docs advertised `internalIds`, but the old API only ever read `internalId` — the old documentation was wrong, not the behavior. Both APIs accept a comma-separated list in it.
- `GET /cors/overview` now honors `labelIds`, `hasTags`, `searchText`, `companyJobNumber`, and `customerReferenceNumbers` independently. The old API silently dropped three of these and applied the other two to the wrong filters.
- `GET /change-notifications`: `fromDueDate` and `untilDueDate` now filter by the Change Notification's due date, as their names say. The old API applied them to the last-update time instead. Use `fromUpdatedAt`/`untilUpdatedAt` if you were relying on the old behavior.
- LMEO Rates: an unrecognized `rateType` path segment returns a 422 validation error. The old API silently served labor rates instead, so a typo returned data that looked valid. Use `labor`, `material`, `equipment`, or `other`.
tags.name: Breaking Changes
